1 .  The applicant-husband who is in custody since 19.06.2023 has approached this Court for grant of regular bail in connection with S.T. No.406 of 2023 arising out of Bishnugarh P.S. Case No.37 of 2022, registered for the offence under Section 304B of IPC, pending in the court of learned Addl.
Sessions Judge-VI, Hazaribag.

2. It has been submitted by learned counsel for the applicant(s) that complete set of F.I.R. alongwith its enclosure have been annexed with this bail application and there is no suppression on his/her part.
3. Innocence have been claimed and undertaking have been given for participation in the trial.
It has been submitted by learned counsel for the applicant that marriage is more than of seven years and as such ingredients of Section 304B of IPC is absent.
Further, it is a case of accidental burn and this applicant has taken her wife to the hospital but she could not survive.
Further, neighbhour has supported the contentions of this applicant.
Earlier U.D. Case was lodged.
Subsequently, after much delay present case has been lodged.
Charge has already been framed.
On above basis prayer for bail has been made.
4. Learned A.P.P. has opposed the prayer for bail of the applicant and submitted that this applicant has criminal antecedent under Section 498A IPC.
It is death by burn injury.

5. It has been replied by learned counsel for the applicant that in Bishnugarh P.S. Case No.29 of 2014 filed under Section 498A of IPC, the applicant has already been bailed out and in Bishnugarh P.S. Case No.95 of 2015 filed under Section 498A of IPC and Sections 3/4 of the D.P. Act, he has Jethu Mahto vs The State Of Jharkhand ....

6. Considering the materials available on record and the cause of death, I am not inclined to enlarge the applicant on bail, at this stage.
Accordingly, prayer for bail of the applicant stands rejected.
7. However, the trial court is directed to conclude the trial within six months.
